title: Kotzig's theorem on light edges of planar graphs
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kotzig's theorem on light edges and its relatives, for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. The weight of an edge uv is deg u + deg v. A planar graph of minimum degree at least three has an edge of weight at most 13 (kotzig_borodin; the form without 3-connectivity conjectured by Erdős and proved by Borodin); a planar graph of minimum degree at least four has an edge of weight at most 11 (light_edge_minDegree_four); Kotzig's theorem (1955): a 3-connected planar graph has an edge of weight at most 13, and at most 11 if it has no vertex of degree three (kotzig); Wernicke's theorem (1904): a planar graph of minimum degree at least five has a vertex of degree five adjacent to a vertex of degree at most six (wernicke). Four statements. The proof is a discharging argument carried out directly on the rotation system, without triangulating.
